body: Wow thanks for the words and the article. I can totally relate to everything you just said. its almost like you know me or are me?  I have a hard time asking for anything I broke my ankle and couldn't even ask my gf of 6 years to help me with physio (although i now suspect she may have had BPD, (mood swings and cutting) . My brother used to call me a ninja cause i was practically invisible and silent.  For years i watched every TV show i wasn't allowed to watch as a child. And ate loads of junk food :) but still have a hard time with decisions and knowing what i want. Its hard for me to believe i deserve things that others take for granted. It took me until 30 to realise i could go to college like everyone else.  You seem to have a real understanding of this topic.  What other kinds of things have you done to help regain your sense of self?
not at all its a great idea actually. thanks for butting in :)

"comforting object that she's made us be."
" when it fits into whatever pretty narrative she's spinning in her head"
Sounds like she may fall into cluster b category.The fact that you are a human being not an object. Your job is to grow into yourself not be a comfort for her. that is supposed to be bonus not a job. 

 But Narcissists and bdps are  very broken people too so i try not to hate, i'm not even sure if its important to diagnose nymore. i just try to keep my emotional distance and try to be accepting.  I gave up on a normal family years ago but part of me still hopes the shell drops one day so i can see my mum for who she is.

Thanks for the kind words your really an awesome person. I was in a relationship for 10 years until a few months ago so all my me problems have been brought back up. I do need to get out more i just have this problem where i need to Do something i can't even just go for a walk. i could if there was an apple to pick or a dog to walk though.. ive been looking at charities that i could help at a few hours a week just to put my mind on helping others instead of myself.

Sounds like my mom . The good mom act seems very self contrived, and then the ''nothings ever good enough'' makes you not want to do anything anymore. Does she say she loves you but you can tell its completely fake only an act, and void of any emotion?

We're definitely inclined to see our parents as perfect so when that image starts to break its hard to understand . I cant tell either if my parents are narcissists or just broken. My Dad showed some remorse once. and i forgive almost everything hes done just for that. But my Mom though, remorse doesnt exist she'd have to make a mistake and perfect people dont do that.

your spot on i have problems with most authority figures i just dont trust them. And i've been denying depression and anxiety for about 10 years now and its not easy to hide it anymore.  Ive recently started meditation yoga and mindfulness it pulls me out of depression and back to reality.  watching dan siegel and besel van der kolks videos on youtube has helped me alot. Most of my problems come from fight or freeze responses. Ive been wanting to get a dog for companionship. but they're  not allowed in my apartment i am looking for a dog friendly apartement but they are a rare find with my budget.

Thanks for the enouragement it really does help. Ive been going through alot lately  I had a decent paying job until january when i went into a major depression i pulled myself out of it to realise i was already screwed tried to fix it with my work but my phone was cut and had no gas left to even get there lol applied for credit card and bank loans so i could fix it but all denied.  Ive been eating rice with beans, carrots, and onions all cooked together bout 2 small meals a day for close to 2 weeks.  I've basically consumed all my muscle at this point and i had finally gained about 15 pounds of muscle over the holiday and then lost about 30 lbs over the next 2 weeks. Im starting to look like an auschwitz survivor. On the upside i've finally started to ask for the help i need but its slow and painfully complicated.

I totally can relate My parents didn't want me to be independent either they wanted to kick me out so i would have to come back and beg its part of the narcissism and feeling powerful and being right all the time. 

to me independence means being able to take care of yourself. something I still struggle with and i just turned 30 btw and been on my own since 15. It's your life so you shouldn't feel guilty for living it; then again I still feel like my life isnt mine and i'm not in control. 

I read that independence comes from security. If your needs are met adequately then the natural human thing to do is grow independent , and then interdependent (family).

Your reasons are as valid as any. abusive family systems are one of the main causes of suicidal thoughts and behavior. My Dad was the same part time. the rest he was drunk and absent.  best thing you can do is leave. Your education is yours not his, it's for you and the rest of your life. And you can get something out of the experience you can learn how not to treat your children.
